workflowChanges: Judge the native profile as its own communication surface. Do not import a prior motion score, require the small avatar to communicate an emotion, or assume website animation is needed to connect the identity.

For future recognition work, expose the real profile naturally and record actual name, avatar, header and project exposure; ask free recall before showing recognition alternatives. Measure name recall, visual recall, maker association and work-category recall separately.

Treat desktop and phone as different exposure paths: the phone begins with a small avatar/name/bio and reaches the large wordmark later. Use actual wheel-scrolled captures; exclude known full-page sticky-navigation artifacts.

When the website exists, compare the same versioned identity in actual GitHub and website contexts. A shared source file is implementation continuity; cross-surface recognition is a separate hypothesis.
Carry only factual public project descriptions and owner-cleared future stories forward. Do not compensate for private work with invented outcomes or an unrequested disclosure.

scoreMeaning: Out of 10: subjective expert judgment of this static local profile’s visual/copy association craft and the written continuity plan. Strong, clear and coherent, with limited distinctive maker evidence and one overconfident recognition phrase. It is not a human recognition/comprehension rate, deployment approval or future website score.
confidence: Moderate-high for visible name hierarchy, copy, thematic consistency and scoped plan quality; moderate for distinctiveness hypotheses. No empirical audience confidence and no live-account verification.
strengths: Nagarjuna Boddu, the heyNag handle/wordmark and “Hey, I’m Nag” form an explicit three-name bridge. At 320px the small avatar is directly beside the full name/handle, with the software bio visible before the README; the association does not depend on the header or a tiny hand gesture.

The universal day avatar retains one face across light and dark GitHub, while the paired headers repeat the same character and wordmark. The desktop and phone previews show a coherent cue system rather than unrelated profile and banner illustrations.

The copy explains software/systems work and three concrete public projects in native readable text. It explicitly describes the public work as a small window, acknowledges private repositories without exposing them, and identifies Grok Bot as unofficial and eva.md as evolving.

The wheel-scrolled 320px README and pins remain readable and consistently name the same destinations. The repeated pin descriptions help connect the conversational project names to their repository slugs; no custom interaction is required to understand or follow them.

The website contract preserves name roles, anatomy, palette, voice, project facts and the chosen Investigate & share behavior. Its planned real-work-first opening, still/reduced-motion paths and absence of a mascot interaction gate are sensible continuity decisions.
The preview is visibly marked unpublished; the unfinished website has no live profile link. The proposal makes no fabricated experience title, numerical impact or private-work showcase claim.

deductions.severity: low to moderate craft opportunity; nonblocking
deductions.classification: Observed content specificity limit; memory effect remains a hypothesis
deductions.finding: The project list communicates what each tool does, but offers little specific evidence of a choice Nag made or a problem he personally pursued. The repeated useful/curious/feel-good framing is coherent but broad. The current page therefore gives stronger category and project-name cues than a distinctive maker story.
deductions.improvementCriterion: If verified public material supports it, add one short concrete reason or design choice to a project, or let its linked repository supply that story. The future website can deepen it through an owner-cleared case study. Do not invent an outcome or disclose private work to satisfy this criterion.
deductions.confidence: High for what the copy contains; moderate for expert distinctiveness judgment; no claim that visitors currently forget Nag.

deductions.severity: low wording issue in the plan; nonblocking
deductions.classification: Design intention phrased more strongly than its evidence
deductions.finding: The continuity plan says the avatar, header and wordmark “establish the shared identity immediately.” The inspected assets provide consistent association cues, but immediacy and cross-surface recognition have not been observed; the future website does not yet exist.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Treat that sentence explicitly as intended identity signaling, and keep actual recognition/transfer unscored until there is a built website and suitable observation. No research recruitment is required for accepting the current local profile.

recommendations: Accept this local profile application as a coherent native GitHub introduction with the named nonblocking limits. Do not infer publication or live account changes from these previews.
Keep the universal avatar, paired headers, native text and three matched public destinations; no new motion or stronger tiny gesture is required for this surface.

Use the future website to add verified personal decisions and richer work evidence while preserving the same name/character relationship. Assess its first visit, reduced-motion path and cross-surface identity only after implementation.

If audience testing is later requested, separate natural branded profile/website memory exposure from isolated unlabeled emotion tests. A profile is supposed to name its maker; its identity copy is not an invalid contaminant for that question.

continuityAssessment.currentProfile: The inspected local preview visibly associates the maker’s names, avatar, wordmark and public work. The claims are appropriately bounded, and native GitHub controls carry the reading/navigation.
continuityAssessment.futurePlan: A credible continuity contract with specific assets, language and behavior to reuse. It is not built artwork, validated first-visit flow or evidence that the two surfaces will be recognized as one maker.
hypotheses: The shared face/unequal antennae and heyNag wordmark will help visitors connect GitHub and the website.
A concrete project decision may create a more distinctive memory of Nag than broad trait language alone.
Investigate & share can elaborate the static curiosity already communicated without taking authorship away from Nag.
continuityAssessment.status: Accept direction; future website quality remains unscored.

unscoredOutcomes.reason: No unfamiliar-human observations or memory outcomes; website is only a plan. No physical-phone, spoken-screen-reader or live account-state certification is implied.
